title.en: Plates release-review rules, rule set 3 (with start check)
title.zh: plates 释放复核规则（第 3 版，含起始状态检查）

description: Rule set 2 (plates-release: same frames, question and per-release rules) plus a start check on the side camera's first frame: a colour already stacked at the start, or with fewer than two plates, is not required. CANDIDATE, validated on development data only (2026-09-29, Qwen3.8-27B, greedy; 63 human-judged episodes: 48 of the rollouts_recap plates pool and the diagnostic set of 15): agreement 0.810 -> 0.921, success recall 0.816 -> 0.959, false successes 3/14 -> 3/14. Known risk: the start check called two separate white plates 'one_or_none' in 11 of about 57 episodes; on an episode whose white plates are never stacked that waiver would give a false success. Not yet checked on a held-out or frozen set.
question:
A robot arm with a two-finger gripper is stacking plates of the same colour (pink on pink, white on white; a green plate is a distractor). The gripper receives an OPEN command at t=0. Images 1-7 are the side camera at t=-2.5, -1.5, -0.8, -0.3, -0.1, +0.4, +1.2 s; images 8-11 are the wrist camera (looking down between the fingers) at t=-1.5, -0.6, -0.1, +0.4 s.
The gripper holds a plate by pinching its thin rim, so a held plate usually hangs TILTED under the fingers; that counts as held if the whole plate is off the table and moves together with the gripper across the earlier images. A plate that stays on the table while the fingers close or drag it is NOT held.
Answer strictly from what the images show:
- held_before: just before the open, is a plate held off the table by the fingers?
- plate_colour: colour of that held plate (none if nothing is held).
- landed_on: after the open, where is that plate: resting on a plate of the same colour, on a plate of another colour, on the table, still in the gripper; nothing_released if no plate was held.
- stays: at t=+1.2 s does it stay where it landed (not sliding off)?
Use unclear whenever the images do not show it.
